implementation_notes: The JDK performs the whole create-or-return: a static final ConcurrentMap<Key, TenantClient> and getInstance(key) returning map.computeIfAbsent(key, TenantClient::new). The docs promise the whole invocation is atomic and the mapping function is invoked exactly once per absent key, while reads stay lock-free; the private constructor keeps the accessor the only path. The mapping function must not update the same map (a recursive registration throws IllegalStateException), and a null result is not stored, so failing factories are re-run on every call.
pitfalls: computeIfAbsent executes the mapping function while holding a bin lock, so a slow construction (network connect, file read) blocks other keys hashing to the same bin; keep it short or move the expensive part behind a per-key lazy slot.
A factory that returns null leaves the key unmapped and the next call retries; fail explicitly instead of returning null.
The static map is per class loader: reloading the class (application server, test runner with separate loaders) creates a second registry, so 'one per key' silently becomes one per loader.

variants.name: Enumerated instances (fixed key set, eager)
variants.idiom_name: enum constants as the key set - one instance per constant
variants.implementation_notes: When the key set is finite and known at compile time, the enum is the registry: each constant is created exactly once by class initialisation under its own lock, is a genuine per-key singleton, and needs no map at all. Lookup becomes valueOf/name, an unknown key fails as IllegalArgumentException instead of creating an entry, and the 'clients cannot add mappings' rule is enforced by the compiler - the strongest form of the pattern, and the form the Wikipedia entry shows for Java.
pitfalls: Eager: every constant and its resources are built at class initialisation even if this run never uses them, and one failing constant fails the whole enum.
Adding a key means recompiling and redeploying; a dynamic key space needs the ConcurrentHashMap form instead.
valueOf throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown keys, so caller-supplied strings need their own validation, and enum constants are per class loader as well.
